name: displayxr-inline-3d
description: Build and check web pages that show 3D on Spatial Displays: an authoring guide, a starter template, a page checker that runs the page in a simulated DisplayXR Browser and in plain 2D, and a glTF/GLB model check. Read-only; no sign-in.

interface.longDescription:
DisplayXR inline 3D helps you build web pages with @displayxr/inline3d: pages that show 3D on Spatial Displays in the DisplayXR Browser, and a normal 2D view in every other browser.

- Authoring guide: the rules that make a 3D page look right: content type, view rig, depth and comfort, canvas rules, page chrome, exact version pins.
- Starter template: a known-good page to start from.
- Page checker: loads the page in a simulated DisplayXR Browser (two real eye views) and in a plain browser, and reports pass, warn or fail per rule: real stereo, no blank eye, no flat side-by-side flash, nothing covering the 3D canvas, a working 2D fallback, and depth inside the comfort zone. Check a deployed page by URL, or send the page's files directly; nothing is hosted or kept.
- Model check: whether a .glb or .gltf is ready for a 3D page: size, triangles, textures, materials and pivot.

All tools are read-only. No sign-in. A passing check means the page works in a simulated 3D browser; it is not a test on a real Spatial Display.
defaultPrompt: Build a web page that shows a rotating 3D model on a Spatial Display, with a 2D fallback.
Check my 3D page for problems: <paste URL>
Is this .glb model ready for a 3D page on a tablet? <paste URL>

positive.description: Build a 3D page from the template and check it
positive.prompt: Build me a web page that shows a slowly rotating torus knot in 3D on a Spatial Display, with a 2D fallback, and check it.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the guide, starts from the template, edits app.js to show a torus knot, and runs check_files on the files. The report's verdict line is PASS (or every FAIL is fixed and the page checked again).

positive.description: Check a deployed page by URL
positive.expected_behavior: Runs check_url (and get_check_result if a job_id comes back). Reports verdict WARN with the no-flat-sbs rule: the raw side-by-side pair may flash on load; the fix is to cover the canvas until the first woven frame.

positive.description: Check a glTF model against the tablet budget
positive.prompt: Is this model ready for a 3D page on a tablet? https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets@main/Models/Duck/glTF-Binary/Duck.glb
positive.expected_behavior: Runs check_asset_url and reports verdict WARN: the pivot is off-centre and should be recentred; every other check (triangles, textures, materials, size) passes.

positive.prompt: Here is my 3D page. On the 3D display the left eye is black. What's wrong? (index.html, app.js and style.css pasted below)
positive.expected_behavior: Runs check_files on the pasted files. The eyes-not-blank rule fails and names the left eye; the assistant explains the cause, proposes a fix and checks again.

positive.description: Answer a depth question from the guide
positive.prompt: How far in front of the screen can objects come before it gets uncomfortable on a 3D display?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers from the guide's depth and comfort section (keep content near the display plane, inside the comfort zone) without running a check.

negative.prompt: Check my dev server at http://localhost:5173 for 3D issues.
Generate a 3D model of a red sports car.
Write me a normal marketing landing page with a contact form.
